posters.name: Pôster principal — A mesa atravessa o tempo
posters.prompt:
Create ONE finished premium theatrical film poster, a single portrait canvas with a 2:3 aspect ratio, high-resolution polished photographic key art with beautifully integrated, impeccably typeset movie-title typography. This is marketing art for an intimate, thoughtful historical time-travel short film: a contemporary man has conversations across five centuries/eras at the same traveling oak table. It is contemplative, mysterious, human, elegant, never a superhero or combat movie.
IDENTITY AND CONTINUITY: Reference image 1 is the real photograph and absolute identity source for Andre Athar. Preserve his recognizable facial geometry, actual age, short textured dark hair with grey at the temples, short salt-and-pepper stubble, natural expression and skin texture. Cinematic lighting/retouch only, no beautification that changes his anatomy, no younger generic actor. Keep his mid-grey pinstripe suit jacket and white finely striped open-collar shirt, no tie. Other references are actual film keyframes and/or the recurring pale weathered oak table: translate their photography, materials, lighting and quiet mood into poster art. Original realistic photography, not painted illustration. Andre is the only person visible. Absolutely NO other human faces, historical portraits, faces in reflections, statues with faces, silhouettes with readable faces, crowd, soldiers, weapons, explosions, clocks, hourglasses or neon sci-fi portals.
TEXT, EXACT SPELLING: The only text is star billing "ANDRE ATHAR", the title "THE TABLE BETWEEN CENTURIES", and a discreet "A SHORT FILM". All text must be highly legible and intentionally art-directed, with the title as the main graphic anchor. The full title must contain exactly those five words, even when split over several lines. Refined film-poster typography, expertly controlled kerning and line spacing; no misspellings, duplicate letters, tiny fake billing blocks, invented reviews, awards, laurels, studios, release dates, watermark or signature. Keep all lettering safely inside the edges. Generate the actual finished poster, no mockup, wall, frame, presentation board or collage of multiple poster designs.

DIRECTION 1 / THEATRICAL HERO. Reference 2 gives the hero at the Galileo table, reference 3 the warm Roman room, reference 4 the oak prop. Build a grand but restrained portrait composition: a large photoreal three-quarter portrait of Andre occupying the upper central two thirds, looking thoughtfully just past the viewer. Below his chest, the pale oak tabletop forms a dramatic perspective line toward a deep arched doorway. Subtly transition the architecture from Tuscan stone on the left to a shadowed red Roman wall on the right, fused into one believable filmic space. A fine shaft of sunlight catches drifting dust, gently connecting epochs; faint cold midnight shadow at the top against burnished amber below. The face is unobscured. Rich black, warm ivory, antique muted gold, subtle film grain. Classically composed prestige theatrical key art. Small widely tracked ANDRE ATHAR at the top. At the bottom, exceptionally beautiful monumental ivory Roman serif title in three lines: "THE TABLE" / "BETWEEN" / "CENTURIES", with CENTURIES largest. A SHORT FILM small underneath. Typography occupies roughly the lower quarter; no title across his face.
